news.title: Claude Code's '/goals' separates the agent that works from the one that decides it's done
news.summary_raw: A code migration agent finishes its run, and the pipeline looks green. But several pieces were never compiled — and it took days to catch. That's not a model failure; that's an agent deciding it was done before it actually was.Many enterprises are now seeing that production AI agent pipelines fail not because of the models’ abilities but because the model behind the agent decides to stop. Several methods to prevent premature task exits are now available from LangChain, Google and OpenA
news.summary: Claude Code migration agent /goals feature lets enterprises detect premature task exits in AI pipelines. This can occur when the agent decides to stop prematurely, unrelated to model abilities.
news.enterprise_use: Check your current AI pipeline automation workflows for potential premature exit points. Review the pipeline execution logs for signs of incomplete tasks. Missing this means manual oversight is required which can delay projects and increase costs. Most affected tool: Freshservice or other ITSM platforms used for incident management.

news.title: mimalloc: A new, high-performance, scalable memory allocator for the modern era
news.summary_raw:
mimalloc is an open-source, modern, scalable memory allocator that is a drop-in replacement for malloc and free. It is relatively small (~12K lines), with clear internal data structures, and is easy to build and integrate into other projects. It provides bounded worst-case allocation times (up to OS primitives), bounded space overhead, low internal fragmentation, and minimal contention by relying almost exclusively on atomic operations.
The post mimalloc: A new, high-performance, scalable memory
news.summary: Microsoft Research has released mimalloc, an open-source, high-performance memory allocator that is a drop-in replacement for malloc and free. This could improve performance and manageability of applications that integrate it.
news.enterprise_use: No high-impact action is directly required, but consider integrating mimalloc in applications with high memory allocation needs to improve performance and memory management.
